steps.title: Look at the two sentences.
steps.prompt: Which word describes the verb — how she does it?
steps.why: An adjective describes a thing or a person. An adverb describes how something is done.

steps.title: Adjectives and adverbs
steps.html:
AdjectiveAdverbExample
carefulcarefullyShe spends it carefully.
quickquicklyHe answered quickly.
dangerousdangerouslyYou're driving dangerously.
quietquietlyWhy are you talking so quietly?
goodwellDid you do well in your exam?
badbadlyThe shop is badly organised.
fast, latefast, lateI get up late at weekends.

steps.title: really, quite, very
steps.html:
WordHow strongExample
quitea littleThe restaurants are quite cheap.
verystrongThese boots are very comfortable.
reallyvery strongIt's a really good price.

These words go before the adjective or the adverb.

Most adverbs are the adjective + -ly. good is the exception: the adverb is well.

Learners often say She drives careful or I did good. Use carefully and well.

items.text: Why are you talking so quietly? — Because we're in the library!
I always get up late at weekends. — Me too, at about ten.
I can't see the television clearly. — I think you need glasses.
Maria answers every question correctly. — She's the best student.
Did you do well in your exam? — I got an 'A'.
